public_rationale: OpenAI’s February 15, 2024 launch disclosure labels physically implausible motion in a Sora running demonstration as a weakness [e1]. This supports the contextual claim that launch-era Sora produced physical errors, beyond merely generating requested imaginary scenes [e1].
limitations: The disclosure establishes the occurrence of errors, not their frequency or how convincing viewers find the outputs.
It does not verify the chessboard dimensions or piece counts.
It does not establish equal error rates or shared error mechanisms between Sora and LLMs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's Sora, like LLMs, makes things up.

statement.excerpt: Turns out Sora makes stuff up, too,

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that Sora can produce realistic-looking depictions containing structural or physical errors. Merely generating an imaginary scene does not count.
The target is the original Sora demonstrated around the post, using the February 15–17, 2024 launch window as the latest publicly observable period.
The comparison with LLMs concerns the existence of errors, not equal error rates or identical mechanisms.
criteria.support_condition: An authenticated launch-era Sora output or contemporaneous developer disclosure establishes an unintended structural or physical error.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes that the alleged examples were misattributed or were requested fictional features, and that the relevant outputs did not contain the claimed class of error.
